summary: Whole-branch codex autoreview (gpt-5.6-sol high, 2-pass chunked, ~587KB bundle) run 3 times to convergence. Round 1 found a real P1 (worker-forgeable jobId could re-scope a grant) - fixed by host-stamping jobId from the spawn registry alongside personId. Round 2 found the registry-miss residual - fixed by keeping the job fail-closed path on a miss. Round 3 re-litigated the two decided tradeoffs; both rejected with rationale pinned inline and in decision 0118.

non_blocking_findings.summary: Rounds 2 and 3 each demanded the residual the other had rejected on the rare registry-miss edge; converged by pinning the chosen residual (keep jobId, fail closed via job lookup) inline.

residual_risks: Registry miss (host restart mid-flight) with a compromised worker forging a group jobId can reach a shared grant - equal to what stripping jobId would produce unconditionally on the same edge; accepted per 0118.
Identity-less DM (memory-ineligible) durable approval writes a shared grant by design (0118): no eligibility gate, no downgrade-to-allow-once.
